clauseStatus.missing: TWO independent, verified gaps, not one: (1) recordFirstJournalAuthorityCommand has zero production callers -- executeCampaignCommand (campaignCommandPipeline.ts:317-322) checks authority.kind === 'journal' and proceeds, but never calls back into the migration marker to record the command that just committed. twoProcessProof.whatTheAcceptanceAsksFor: roadmap.json's second acceptance line for this node: 'Real durable source/restart and two-process scoped convergence before cutover acceptance; no E2E-only flag used as production proof.' Read together with e2e/campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's own footer (lines 434-461), this is not a hypothetical ask -- the closest existing test already documents, in production code comments, that it cannot be driven today.
whatWouldBeNeeded: A real second OS process (spawn('node', ['server.js'], { env: { PORT, DATABASE_PATH, ... } })) pointed at its OWN SQLite file -- e2e/campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts:41-106 (startSecondServer) is a directly reusable pattern, already proven to boot a second server with its own database.

A campaign whose marker is already in 'journal' state with a non-empty journal stream on BOTH processes' shared or replicated storage -- today this requires either (a) flipping isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() via the e2e-only env var (which the acceptance explicitly forbids treating as production proof), or (b) a test-scoped direct call to importCampaignBaseline + advanceAfterShadowParity + writeCampaignMigrationMarker against a real SQLite file, bypassing the flag entirely by calling the pure/marker-store functions directly the way campaignAuthorityBlocked.test.ts already does for the single-process case.

A real write on process A (through POST /commands, which requires authority.kind==='journal' -- satisfiable via (b) above) followed by a real read on process B against the same or a replicated database file, asserting B's projection reflects A's committed event without any in-memory sharing between the two Node processes.

A real OS-level restart of at least one process mid-scenario (kill and respawn, reusing scripts/e2e/relaunching-server.mjs's spawn/respawn pattern) with a re-read afterward, to fold the 'restart' half of the acceptance into the same proof rather than leaving it as a separate in-process-only test.
twoProcessProof.minimumHonestRuntimeProof: One new e2e (or scripts/qc) spec, modeled directly on campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's process-spawning shape, that (1) uses the marker-store/journal functions directly (not the production flag) to put a campaign on real journal authority against a real SQLite file, (2) spawns a second real server process pointed at the SAME database file (not a separate one -- convergence via a shared durable store is the property under test, distinct from the existing spec's separate-file replica-sync scenario), (3) commits a command via POST /commands on process A, (4) reads the campaign via GET /api/campaigns/[id] on process B and asserts the committed event is visible, and (5) kills and respawns one process mid-scenario to fold in the restart proof. This does NOT require flipping CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED in production -- it only requires the test harness to construct a journal-state marker directly, exactly as campaignAuthorityBlocked.test.ts already does for its single-process cases.
twoProcessProof.cost: Estimated 1 new spec file (~150-250 lines, following campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's existing ~460-line pattern for process lifecycle) plus no production code changes if the existing marker/journal functions are sufficient -- BUT the compatibleRollback gap (recordFirstJournalAuthorityCommand never called) means a two-process proof that also exercises rollback mid-scenario would surface that gap immediately, so a slice ordering that proves basic convergence FIRST and rollback SEPARATELY (after the wiring gap is fixed) is recommended over one large spec.
twoProcessProof.existingAllGreenDoesNotSubstitute: verify:qc:multiplayer-reliability and the other frozen CAMP-01 journeys referenced elsewhere in roadmap.json exercise co-op SYNC (transport, grants, delivery), never the campaign-authority migration-state machine, because CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED is false in every one of those runs -- confirmed by campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's own footer citing the same flag as the reason convergence cannot be driven.

ownerGatedParts.od_flushMechanism_doesNotApply: roadmap.json's OD-flush-mechanism is scoped to node 'R2.authority-client' task 1.6 (fetch-keepalive-on-pagehide vs sendBeacon for flushing an in-flight client write on navigation-discard). ownerGatedParts.actualGate_singlePlayerIdentity: The real owner-blocked dependency for PRODUCTION cutover (not discovery) is the recorded 2026-09-15T09:56:02.105Z owner decision ('single-player identity/seat for campaign commands (6.2b + OB-2)', roadmap.json ownerDecisions[]): POST /api/campaigns/[id]/commands requires an active campaign_session_participant row (isActiveCampaignSeat, CampaignSessionParticipantStore.ts:255-269), which only a co-op session creates. A single-player campaign -- the majority case -- has no participant row and therefore no path to /commands under ANY migration state, flag value, or marker content. Even a fully-wired, fully-tested, fully-flipped cutover would only ever activate for co-op campaigns until this identity gap is resolved. This brief does not recommend flipping it and none of the proposed slices require it (the two-process proof constructs journal-authority markers directly, bypassing the flag, exactly as the existing single-process test already does).
whatIsDeliverableWithoutAnyFlagFlipOrOwn: Wiring recordFirstJournalAuthorityCommand into executeCampaignCommand's success path (closes the compatibleRollback gap) -- pure code change plus tests, no flag touch, no identity model needed.

A shadow-parity DRIVER (scheduled job, admin-only endpoint, or CLI script) that calls the already-correct runCampaignShadowParity for campaigns in 'shadowing' -- needs a design decision on WHERE it runs (cron vs on-demand vs admin route) but not an owner ruling on identity or the production flag.
The two-process convergence + restart proof described above, built entirely against test-constructed journal-state markers.
A rollback OPERATIONAL surface (script or admin route) exposing rollbackToSnapshotAuthority, now that it would have real data to act on.

None of this requires single-player identity or a production flag flip; it only requires the campaign under test to already hold a co-op session (which the existing two-device spec's fixtures already construct).
